verses.pali: “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, mahāsamuddo parikkhayaṁ pariyādānaṁ gaccheyya, ṭhapetvā dve vā tīṇi vā udakaphusitāni.
verses.english: “Mendicants, suppose the water in the ocean dried up and evaporated except for two or three drops.

verses.pali: katamaṁ nu kho bahutaraṁ, yaṁ vā mahāsamudde udakaṁ parikkhīṇaṁ pariyādiṇṇaṁ yāni vā dve vā tīṇi vā udakaphusitāni avasiṭṭhānī”ti?
verses.english: Which is more: the water in the ocean that has dried up and evaporated, or the two or three drops left?”

verses.pali: “Etadeva, bhante, bahutaraṁ mahāsamudde udakaṁ, yadidaṁ parikkhīṇaṁ pariyādiṇṇaṁ;
verses.english: “Sir, the water in the ocean that has dried up and evaporated is certainly more.

verses.pali: appamattakāni dve vā tīṇi vā udakaphusitāni avasiṭṭhāni.
verses.english: The two or three drops left are tiny.

verses.pali: Neva satimaṁ kalaṁ upenti na sahassimaṁ kalaṁ upenti na satasahassimaṁ kalaṁ upenti mahāsamudde udakaṁ parikkhīṇaṁ pariyādiṇṇaṁ upanidhāya dve vā tīṇi vā udakaphusitāni avasiṭṭhānī”ti.
verses.english: Compared to the water in the ocean that has dried up and evaporated, it’s not nearly a hundredth, a thousandth, or a hundred thousandth part.”
“In the same way, for a noble disciple, the suffering that’s over and done with is more …”
